text:
A: Hello! Hi, can you hear me? I thought we'd finished, sorry, I'd started making Esi's snack.
B: Oh, gosh, so did I. Hello. I'm Joanne.
A: Akosua. Hi, Joanne. Is that your dog at the bottom of the screen?
B: Yes, Biscuit. He's slept through all five calls. He's the only one who's relaxed about it.
A: Ha! Can I say something, is that okay? When I saw your photo I thought, oh, she's so organised, with the box files and everything. I bet her paperwork's perfect.
B: Oh, gosh, no. Honestly, no. My inbox is a disaster. I've got about two hundred flagged emails. The box files are mostly empty, I think I just bought them hoping it would help.
A: No! Oh, that makes me feel so much better. I was in HR, and my paperwork was always piling up. I had a colleague who used to chase me for everything.
B: Was? Have you moved on?
A: Erm. Redundancy. Eight months ago, they did a restructure. I'm job hunting now. Slowly, to be honest. Sorry, I keep saying that to everyone.
B: No, don't apologise. That must have been awful. What sort of thing are you looking for?
A: Something like before. Employee relations, the difficult conversations. Council or housing, ideally. Part-time or hybrid, because of the school run.
B: Erm, councils do advertise those quite a lot, actually. Ours had an HR advisor post up last month, I think. I'm not saying that very helpfully, sorry, but they do exist. And the hybrid thing is quite normal now. I'm three days at home.
A: Really? Okay, that's good to hear. I've been looking mostly at housing associations. I'll add councils to my tabs. I've got too many tabs.
B: I'm a planner, and honestly I think it's a bit like your job. People are upset about something, a neighbour's extension or whatever, and you have to tell them straight what's happening. I'm fine one to one. It's the committee meetings I dread. I get a knot in my stomach for days.
A: Yes! One to one, I'm fine. Stand me in front of a room and I'm shaking. Is your family nearby? Sorry, random question.
B: Erm, my mum's in Andover, not far. She's getting a bit forgetful, actually. I worry I don't go enough.
A: Oh, I'm sorry. My mum lives with us, and she's getting older, her knee's bad. She talks about going back to Ghana. I don't know what I'd do. Sorry, that's a lot.
B: No, I understand. It's hard, isn't it, watching them get older.
A: It is. I pray about it, honestly. That's what gets me through.
B: I think whatever helps. I just walk the dog round the same loop and overthink.
A: Ha! That's my friend and me round Norwood Grove. Supposed to be exercise, really just talking.
B: I think that counts. I think we're nearly out of time.
A: Okay. Joanne, thank you, honestly. I'm going to look at the councils tonight.
B: Good luck. I really hope you find something.
